How my book hit #1 in the world on Amazon (and the writing technique that made the book sticky)

Written by
Vishen
Share
Share on X Share on Facebook Share on LinkedIn
5
7
Share
5
7
5
Share on X Share on Facebook Share on LinkedIn

So in 2017, my book hit number #1 on Amazon for a very strange reason.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:11
Instaread

This is a story about the Dalai Lama and vodka shots, and how those two ideas came together to push my book to number #1 on Amazon. 

And I don’t mean number #1 in a category, like personal growth for men over forty who own Labradors. I mean number one in every category, across all of Amazon, which briefly made me the number #2 author in the world, ahead of Tolkien and his combined works, and J.K. Rowling and her combined works (yes, every Harry Potter book, together). Here are the screenshots to prove it.

The book hit #1 on Amazon Sep 16, 2017

The book stayed as a top book on Amazon for the next 3 months (screenshot taken on Nov 11, 2027) , periodically bouncing back to the #1 spot across all books on Amazon.

Briefly making me the #2 Author in the world (ahead of even JK Rowling and Tolkien for a few brief days)

Now let me tell you how it happened, and why I’m sharing this with you, especially today.

So the book opens in a hotel bar in Calgary, 2009. In a few hours, I’m going on stage right after the Dalai Lama, in the slot they keep for the speaker nobody came to see, and I’m so nervous that a shot of vodka from the lobby bar feels like a professional decision.

Now think about that for a second. A holy man and a shot glass. Those two things do not belong in the same sentence, and the moment they are, your brain needs to know how it ends. Do I embarrass myself? Do I get banned from Tibet? Does His Holiness join me for one? You turn the page. 

And by the time you’ve found out, I’ve started something else you need to finish.

That’s called an idea collision.

Idea collision: two ideas that don’t belong together, forced into one story.

And here’s the thing. It wasn’t the only one. When I went back through the first eleven pages of that book (The Code of the Extraordinary Mind), I found a whole system in there that I’d built without knowing I was building it. 

There’s a move I call the unsell, where I tell you on page one that you might hate this book, and the reader who was about to drift has just been dared to stay. There’s the thing you can’t unsee, a promise that the book will change you, not inform you. 

There are open loops, every one with an address, a chapter number where it closes. There’s phraseology, the new words, more than twenty of them, so you have a handle to carry each idea out of the room by. And there’s the slippery slope, short sentences where each one makes the next unavoidable.

Now, why eleven? Because every so often Amazon gives a book away free to thousands of its premium members, and most of those books get skimmed and shelved, so Amazon only counts a book as read once you get past page eleven. Amazon didn’t read my book. It counted. And almost everyone who opened it got past page eleven, because that’s where the system lives. The ranking had to move. It moved all the way to the top.

Let that sink in for a second.

The ideas got the book written. The system got it read.

And I believe this is the thing nobody teaches experts. 

You spent years getting good at your idea. Nobody spent one afternoon showing you how to make a person turn the page. It’s not luck, and it’s not talent. There’s a structure. And once you see it, you can’t unsee it.

So here’s why I’m telling you this today. 

At the Expert to Authority Summit, starting this Friday (Sep 18), I break the whole thing down. Not just how to write a book that’s sticky. How to build courses, content, and books that people finish, that turn readers into fans.

This is how Mindvalley has accumulated 26,000 case studies from students who willingly share their stories of transformation.

Here’s what happens in the room.

Friday: Sep 18

I open with why most experts stay invisible. Marisa Peer on the moment she stopped being a practitioner and became an authority. Then you draft your own signature method, live, name and all. It will be rough. That’s the point.

Saturday: Sep 19

One idea turned into thirty days of content, built live with AI. The email machine. The product step ladder. Ajit Nawalkha takes four to six people through their positioning and their method name, on stage, in front of everyone.

Sunday: Sep 20

Daniel Priestley on the weekly cadence that builds an audience whether you feel like it or not. The funnel that runs without you on the call. Regan Hillyer, fireside. Then I take real expert funnels apart, live.

The full curriculum, all twenty sessions, is here so you know exactly what we’re covering:

Now, who is this for? Four people.

The founder with a hot product who understands they have to be the face of it. 

The expert who’s hit a ceiling: you have the audience, you have the book, and you’re coasting, and you can’t work out how to go bigger. 

The expert who is brilliant and has no audience at all. 

And, the person who already has an audience and has no idea how to turn it into a living.

If you’re one of those four, this is where you learn to build the funnels, the courses, and the training systems your audience will want to pay you to learn.

48 hours left: Claim your free spot

Friday 18 to Sunday 20 September, live on Zoom, free, no replay.
Starts: 8am Los Angeles / 11am New York/ 4pm London /7pm Dubai /8:30pm Delhi /11pm Singapore.

I hope to see you there.

PS: If an idea in this article resonated with you, tell me what you’re excited to learn this weekend at the Expert to Authority Summit by leaving a comment. I read every single comment.

Fact-Checking: Our Process

Mindvalley is committed to providing reliable and trustworthy content. 

We rely heavily on evidence-based sources, including peer-reviewed studies and insights from recognized experts in various personal growth fields. Our goal is to keep the information we share both current and factual. 

The Mindvalley fact-checking guidelines are based on:
  • Content Foundation: Our articles build upon Mindvalley’s quest content, which are meticulously crafted and vetted by industry experts to ensure foundational credibility and reliability.
  • Research and Sources: Our team delves into credible research, ensuring every piece is grounded in facts and evidence, offering a holistic view on personal growth topics.
  • Continuous Updates: In the dynamic landscape of personal development, we are committed to keeping our content fresh. We often revisit and update our resources to stay abreast of the latest developments.
  • External Contributions: We welcome insights from external contributors who share our passion for personal transformation and consciousness elevation.
  • Product Recommendations and Affiliations: Recommendations come after thoughtful consideration and alignment with Mindvalley’s ethos, grounded in ethical choices.

To learn more about our dedication to reliable reporting, you can read our detailed editorial standards.
